import math


def test_greatest_common_divisor():
    # Basic cases
    assert greatest_common_divisor(3, 5) == 1
    assert greatest_common_divisor(25, 15) == 5
    assert greatest_common_divisor(48, 18) == 6
    assert greatest_common_divisor(12, 36) == 12

    # Coprime numbers
    assert greatest_common_divisor(17, 13) == 1
    assert greatest_common_divisor(101, 103) == 1

    # Equal numbers
    assert greatest_common_divisor(7, 7) == 7
    assert greatest_common_divisor(100, 100) == 100

    # Zero handling
    assert greatest_common_divisor(0, 5) == 5
    assert greatest_common_divisor(5, 0) == 5
    assert greatest_common_divisor(0, 0) == 0

    # One divides the other
    assert greatest_common_divisor(10, 50) == 10
    assert greatest_common_divisor(50, 10) == 10

    # Larger numbers (classic Euclid example)
    assert greatest_common_divisor(1071, 462) == 21

    # Negative inputs (result magnitude should match positive gcd)
    assert abs(greatest_common_divisor(-48, 18)) == 6
    assert abs(greatest_common_divisor(48, -18)) == 6
    assert abs(greatest_common_divisor(-48, -18)) == 6

    # Cross-check against math.gcd on a range of values
    for x in range(0, 50):
        for y in range(0, 50):
            assert abs(greatest_common_divisor(x, y)) == math.gcd(x, y)

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_greatest_common_divisor()
